hook_text: South Africa's cheapest power station cost nothing to build, burns nothing, and you can switch it on tonight.
clip_script: Everyone draws South Africa's energy crisis as an empty tap: not enough power stations. Redraw it. It is a leaking bucket — plenty pours in at the top while streams escape through holes on every side: draughty buildings, ancient bulbs, uninsulated geysers, worn-out motors, lights burning in empty offices. Now the money question. A new power station costs hundreds of billions of rand and takes a decade to build. Plugging holes — insulation, LEDs, geyser timers, efficient motors — costs a fraction, works within months, and emits absolutely nothing. That is why engineers call efficiency the INVISIBLE power station: the station you never have to build, because the demand it would have served no longer exists. Now zoom into your own house at six in the evening — the moment the national grid groans hardest. That evening peak is not made by factories; it is millions of kitchens switching on together: geysers, stoves, kettles, heaters. A stadium wave is just individuals lifting their arms — and it circles the whole stadium. So run the big plays in order. The geyser first — it drinks around 40 per cent of the bill: thermostat to 60, blanket, timer, solar if you can. Then LEDs: same light, one tenth of the power. Lids on pots. Kill the little red standby eyes that drink all night. Government writes the rules, business turns the big bolts — but the wave is sixty million households, and the champion stays the same: the kilowatt-hour you never use.
visual_style: A bucket of light leaking glowing streams labelled with household culprits, holes sealing one by one; a translucent 'invisible' power station fading in beside a real one with price tags; a stadium wave morphing into rows of houses switching to warm efficient light at dusk.
pacing: Punchy reframe at the open, satisfying hole-plugging rhythm, building wave energy to a calm, certain close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and rank every energy fix in your own home by size.
